body:
## ⚠ IN-FLIGHT STATE (2026-08-23): STRIPPED FOR PUBLISH — awaiting "return to build mode"

The workspace tree is runtime-only: About/ Assemblies/ Languages/ Textures/ LICENSE
(+ `.git`/`.gitignore`/`.modmixer` deliberately in place). The game-side junction points at
the workspace as normal. **`Source/` (51 .cs + csproj) is at
`D:\Rimworld\Radius UI Framework\20260823-122935\Source\`** and the full pre-strip tree is
pushed as git tag **`source-20260823-122935`** on `Astryls/Radius-UI-Framework`.

**The publish protocol (user-stated, authoritative — the junction-swap idea from earlier this
session was WRONG and has been reverted):**
1. On strip: MOVE Source/ and non-runtime components to a versioned backup
   `D:\Rimworld\<Mod Name>\<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>\` AND push a backup (tag) to the mod's GitHub.
2. The user publishes **via Modmixer** (not the in-game uploader).
3. When the user says **"return to build mode"**: assume published, MOVE the files back into
   the workspace, KEEPING the D:\ versioned backup and the tag.

Restore command when told: `mv "/d/Rimworld/Radius UI Framework/20260823-122935/Source" .`
(then verify 51 .cs files back, build NOT required - Assemblies/ never moved).

**Autosave caveat:** ModmixerGitAutosave commits every 15 min and is NOT disabled (the old
prep script did that; no tool for it now). If the publish window runs long, an autosave will
commit the stripped tree - recoverable (tag + D: backup hold everything; restoring Source and
the next autosave heals HEAD) but it creates a delete/restore commit pair. Keep the window
short.

## What this mod is

A **library mod**. It adds no defs, no world state, and no Harmony patches. It exists so the
Radius UI suite draws with one design language instead of many forked copies of one.

**The About.xml Harmony dependency is INTENTIONAL despite zero code references** (verified: no
HarmonyLib in Source/ or csproj). ARCHITECTURE's header documents it as a load-order anchor:
`Harmony -> Framework -> consumers` means a consumer only declares the framework. Do not
"fix" it away.

Design language: flat 2.0, rounded, iOS-like, colour-forward.

Architecture of record: `_dev/RadiusUIFramework/ARCHITECTURE.md` (human-owned; agent-amended
2026-08-23 to gen 9 with a §12 change-log row). Nothing in `_dev/` ships.

## Status: generation 9, third release stripped + ready (Workshop 3786107692)

Last shipped generation was 5 (2026-08-20). This release ships generations 6-9:

- **Gen 6** - radial vocabulary (`Spatial.Arc`, `Palette.Commands`, `SizeAnim`).
- **Gen 7** - the World layer becomes assertable (additive, no code moved).
- **Gen 8** - `WorldSnapshot.Get` seed/window fix. **Breaking signature change.**
- **Gen 9** - `RadiusFont.LabelItalic` (additive, bumped per the generation rule, which has
  now cost user-facing crashes THREE times). LabelItalic users assert 9; World/ users assert 8.
- Also in this release: the overview-tab standard (`Metrics.Tabs` + `Panes/OverviewTab`).

Shipped DLL verified by decompile: `FrameworkVersion.Current = 9`, Release, no pdb.
Git: `Astryls/Radius-UI-Framework` (private), `main`. Licence MIT.

### PUBLISH_CHECKLIST state (../_dev/PUBLISH_CHECKLIST.md) as of 2026-08-23

- **§1 Content freeze: GREEN** (zero em/en dashes About+Keyed+new docs; keyed strings verified;
  LabelItalic added no strings).
- **§2 Documentation: GREEN** - ARCHITECTURE.md at gen 9; `STEAM_DESCRIPTION.txt` +
  `UPDATE_NOTES.txt` authored (house BBCode style + Quality Commitment block);
  `HELICOPTER_VIEW.md` regenerated via the generic
  `../_dev/RadiusUISocialTab/generate-helicopter-view.sh` (pass the mod path). No field
  manual: library mod, no mechanics.
- **§3 Assets: GREEN** (Preview 1280x720, ModIcon, 272 PNGs, no strays).
- **§4 Metadata: description rewrite drafted but NOT applied** (user owns it; draft mirrors
  STEAM_DESCRIPTION.txt). packageId deviates from `astryl.<PascalCaseName>` but is immutable
  post-publish.
- **§5 Build/clean load: GREEN** - two bridge-monitored isolated loads, zero errors; plus a
  stripped-tree load test passed (Player.log, zero error/exception lines).
- **§6 Strip: DONE per protocol** (see in-flight banner).
- **§7 Performance: GREEN** - Dubs session 2026-08-23, user sign-off.

### Pdb recurrence (structural fix is Release-only)

The csproj `DebugType=none` guard is conditioned on Release and OutputPath ignores
configuration, so ANY Debug build re-drops `RadiusUI.Framework.pdb` into `Assemblies/`,
invisible to git. One from 08-22 was deleted 08-23. Tell: DLL mtime newer than pdb mtime =
last build was Release. Check `Assemblies/` before every publish.

**Do not trust a literal-only grep to condemn a keyed string.** The 11 apparent orphans are all
live: 8 accent names resolve through `("RadiusUI.Accent." + name).Translate()` and 3 more take
`.Translate(arg)`. **Build Release explicitly** - `dotnet build` defaults to Debug and silently
replaces the shipping DLL.

**Sync drift warnings are expected, permanently.** `.modmixer/cs-assets.json` declares all 272
icon paths; `RadiusIcon`/`IconSet` build paths from constants, so every sync warns "declared
but no literal matches" for every icon. Correct as designed - never remove the entries.

## Texture library (272 icons, 19 categories)

Imported from five source mods, byte-for-byte: no resampling, no recolouring.

Namespaced under `Textures/RadiusUI/` because `ContentFinder` returns the *last-loaded* match,
so an un-namespaced sibling in a consumer would silently shadow it. Consumers must delete their
local copies, not merely stop referencing them.

### The art is three tiers, not one family

Only tier 1 can be re-themed:

- **Glyphs** - flat white RGB, all information in alpha. Tinted via `Palette`/accent.
- **Illustrations (`Anatomy/`)** - shaded beige art. Never tinted.
- **Semantic markers (`Marker/`)** - colour *is* the meaning. Hand synced to the palette: if the
  ramp changes, those 8 PNGs must be re-authored.

### Aliases are a hard requirement

12 retired names must stay exposed or consumer call sites break. `Squad/` ships 5 files but
offers 8 emblem slots; `Reminder/` ships 7 but offers 8 picker slots. `Action/LockOpen` and
`Action/LockClosed` scored 0.927 similarity and were deliberately kept apart - a **state pair**.

**No magnifier/search glyph exists**, deliberately: `FlatField` ships with no leading icon
rather than misusing `Action/EyeOpen`.

## Components

- `Tokens/` - `Palette` (+ Health, Ideology, Needs, Social, Bands, Commands partials), `Metrics`
  (+ Rows, Tabs partials). Pure values, no game state.
- `Chrome/` - `CardChrome`, `FlatField`, `Spatial` (+ Bands, Arc partials), `SizeAnim`.
- `Widgets/` - `FlatScroll`, `UIKit` (+ Bars partial).
- `Panes/OverviewTab` - standard tab footprint + live pane clamp.
- `Icons/` - `RadiusIcon` (art tier lives here), `IconSet` + generated per-tier partials.
- `Text/RadiusFont` - framework-owned font resolution and measurement. Gen 9 adds `LabelItalic`
  (explicit-weight italic twin of `LabelBold`; real italic face only on dynamic fonts, bitmap
  falls back to regular).
- `World/WorldSnapshot` - real-terrain minimap bake + `TerritoryPaint`.
- `Settings/`, `Compat/ModCompat`, `Perf/`.

Several classes are `partial` (`Spatial`, `UIKit`, `Metrics`, `Palette`, `IconSet`) so
concurrent sessions add a **file** instead of editing a shared one.

### `World/WorldSnapshot` - real-terrain minimap bake (section 16)

Bounded BFS from a centre tile, rasterising each tile's actual polygon onto the tangent plane.
768squared `Color32`, ~2.3 MB reused, ~5 ms upload, cached on centre/range/orientation/window/paint.

`TerritoryPaint` is **immutable** to the bake: a changed claim map must arrive as a new `Key` or
the cache returns a stale texture. Use `Transport` across a re-centre; deriving the basis from a
fixed world axis makes north swing and reads as the map rotating. Terrain colours are map
**content**, so this file does not route through `Palette`.

**Gen 8 fix (the blank-map bug).** `Get` separates the projection origin from the baked
`window`, so a caller can pan without re-projecting (moving the origin warps the picture; moving
the window just slides which part of the same projection is baked). `seed` moved from
`PlanetTile = default` to `PlanetTile? = null`: `PlanetTile.Valid` is `tileId >= 0` and Invalid
is -1, so `default(PlanetTile)` - tileId **0** - tested as VALID. Every caller omitting the seed
flood-filled from tile 0, failed the window cull on its first iteration, enqueued nothing and
got back the `WaterColor` pre-fill. It presented as "the world map is blank" when it was really
the untouched buffer.

### `Panes/OverviewTab` - the standard tab footprint (section 17)

**Every module replacing a vanilla overview tab renders at the same size.** Standard is
`Metrics.OverviewTabW` x `OverviewTabH` = **890 x 790** at scale 1, user scale clamped
**0.70-1.10** defaulting to **1.00**, height clamped against the live inspect pane.

Audit (2026-08-20): Health and Needs matched at 890x790 @1.00, but **Social Tab had its axes
transposed** (790x890 @0.85, rendering 672x756) - right numbers, swapped axes. Invisible in
isolation, obvious side by side.

The helper also owns the **clamp** (the limit must come from live `PaneTopY` because RimHUD and
other pane mods raise it, and `UI.screenHeight` is already divided by `Prefs.UIScale`) and the
**default scale**.

**Hosted-tab trap:** a tab whose rect is owned by a host (Radius UI - Inspector) must use
`MaxHeightHosted(chromeH)`, never `MaxHeight` - clamping against `PaneTopY` there clamps against
your own output; the chase is the flicker.

### `Chrome/FlatField` - the flat text field

Framework-owned because it is **shared-GUIStyle surgery**. `Widgets.TextField` draws with
`Text.CurTextFieldStyle`, whose eight state backgrounds are vanilla's tan bevel, so a consumer's
own plate goes *under* vanilla chrome. The fix is a copy of that style with all eight nulled.

Four encoded rules: never mutate the shared style (`GUI.skin.textField` is a pure no-op -
`Widgets.TextField` never reads it); copy from `Text.textFieldStyles[Small]`, not
`CurTextFieldStyle`, which resolves against ambient `Text.Font`; cache behind an epoch guard on
both the source style object and its font; `GUI.SetNextControlName` immediately before
`GUI.TextField` or focus detection silently never matches.

The clear button's `ButtonInvisible` and 24px reserve are emitted whenever `clearButton` is
true, not only when non-empty: a control appearing mid-frame renumbers every later control.

### `Chrome/Spatial` - the shape module (section 15)

What `CardChrome` structurally cannot draw. Generated textures only, no shipped art.

Cost discipline: a 9-slice is nine draw calls - surfaces and row cards only; `Pill` is three;
faint row stripes stay square. `Pill` samples **half** discs by texcoord because whole discs
under a rect double-draw the caps. `BottomBand` clips rather than shrinks. All textures are
`HideAndDontSave` or `UnloadUnusedAssets` destroys them mid-session.

`Spatial.Arc` (gen 6): one cached texture per **shape** (inner ratio + sweep), rotated to
bearing. Angle convention **0 = up, clockwise**, and `AngleFromUp`/`InSector` ship WITH the
drawing so a consumer's hit shape cannot drift from the drawn shape. Rotation must use
`Verse.UI.RotateAroundPivot`, never `GUIUtility.RotateAroundPivot` - the latter reads its pivot
in SCREEN space, invisible at UI scale 1.0 and scattering wedges at any other scale.

### `Perf/` - hot-path utilities

`FrameGate`, `Throttle`, `TextMemo`, `ScratchText`, `SnapshotTable`, `IdMap`,
`PooledWindowState`, `ViewCull`, `PatchGuard`, `DefTable`, `FrameProbe`. Main-thread only.
`RadiusFont.Size/Height/Width` route through `TextMemo` behind unchanged signatures.

**Threading/DrawBatch review (2026-08-23): main-thread-only is a design decision, not an
omission.** Verified in 1.6 source: `DrawBatch` is world-space mesh accumulation (fleck
pipeline) - inapplicable to an IMGUI-only suite. Stat lookups are NOT safe off-thread
(`StatWorker.temporaryStatCache` is a plain Dictionary written on read). The only eligible
compute block is the WorldSnapshot BFS bake (~5 ms, cached, upload main-thread anyway): stays
synchronous; if Dubs ever shows it as a real hitch, time-slice the BFS before considering
threads. Lore saved under `performance`.

## Binding rules for framework edits (section 13)

Additive only; never change the value behind an existing name; missing token means add a new
one; **rebuild every consumer after any framework rebuild** and hash-verify their game-side
copies; the 12 icon aliases are permanent; rule 6 - any vanilla-overview-tab replacement uses
`Panes/OverviewTab`. Prefer a new `partial` file over editing a shared one. Always re-read a
file from disk immediately before editing it, **including ARCHITECTURE.md**.

**Generation rule (has now cost user-facing crashes THREE times):** a consumer must require the
first generation **that cannot predate the members it uses** - not the generation current when
it was written (`Epoch` inside 3, World/ inside 6, LabelItalic would have hidden inside 8).
World/ users assert **8** (Get's signature moved there); `LabelItalic` users assert **9**.

## Outstanding work (next session starts here)

1. **On "return to build mode": move Source back** from
   `D:\Rimworld\Radius UI Framework\20260823-122935\` (keep the backup + tag), verify 51 .cs.
2. **About.xml `<description>` rewrite** drafted in STEAM_DESCRIPTION.txt, never applied
   (user's call).
3. **Radius UI - World Map still under-asserts** (requires 6, uses `WorldSnapshot.BiomeColor`;
   DLL post-dates gen 8 so not a live crash). Move its assertion to 8 and rebuild at its next
   session. Consumer-side.
4. **Social Tab must be re-pointed at the standard footprint** (renders 672x756 vs standard
   890x790) - visible change, needs sign-off. Consumer-side.
5. **Health and Needs should migrate to `Panes/OverviewTab`** (no visible change). Consumer-side.
6. **Faction Menu still carries two forks** the framework owns: `Chrome/FlatField.cs` and
   `Source/Core/WorldSnapshot.cs`. Consumer-side.

Game-side `Mods/RadiusUIFramework` is a **junction** to the workspace: builds land in place,
and RimWorld must be closed before building or the DLL is write-locked through the junction.
